title: [GMCP 203.016.04] Adversarial and failure behavior: First-class extension framework and extension governance
goal: Requirement GMCP-203-016-04. Close validation, authorization, isolation, privacy, bounded-resource, cancellation, concurrency, crash, retry, rollback, and recovery behavior. Add deterministic negative, attack, race, corruption, and fault-injection fixtures derived from the vector threat model. Vector outcome: Namespaced MCP extensions can be discovered, negotiated, configured, versioned, isolated and disabled through one typed framework without forking core protocol code. Unknown extensions round-trip safely, required unsupported extensions fail explicitly, official and experimental status is visible, collision and downgrade rules are enforced, and a watch process opens roadmap work for every newly published official extension. Done means production-path tests and retained evidence prove this work package; task closure or roadmap wording alone is not evidence.
